item.title: 🟠 GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality-system impact — consider guest services, PMS/POS, and property operations.
A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 4h

item.title: 🟠 Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
item.description:
Why this matters: Useful IT context for operational and leadership awareness.
Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup,

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 4h

item.title: 🔴 CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.
The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

item.title: 🟠 Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect sign-ins, MFA, or Conditional Access — watch for authentication issues.
A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. Fixed kernels shipped

item.description:

Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine. The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker

item.description:

When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.
